newsitem.title: GREECE: SOCCER-LOKO HAT-TRICK SENDS PSG IN TO SEMIS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LOKO HAT-TRICK SENDS PSG IN TO SEMIS.

text.p: French international striker Patrice Loko scored a hat-trick on Thursday to give defending champions Paris St Germain a 3-0 away victory over AEK Athens and a place in the semifinals of the European Cup Winners' Cup.
It is the fifth successive season PSG have reached a European semifinal.

PSG shook off the poor form haunting them for much of the season - including the goalless first leg in Paris - to dominate Thursday's tie with Loko and Brazilian Leonardo often spreading panic in the Greek defence.
Midfielder Paul Le Guen crashed a shot against the woodwork after 20 minutes as PSG signalled their attacking intentions.
And two minutes later Loko got the opener when he seized on a cross by Jerome Leroy to beat goalkeeper Ilias Atmatsidis from 10 metres.
Loko claimed his second just before half time, converting a pass by Leonardo, to shatter the hopes of AEK's 28,000 fervent fans.

The Greeks had high hopes of a first European semifinal for 20 years after holding PSG to a goalless draw in Paris. But their only effort of note in the first half was a shot by Georgian Timour Ketspagia which flew wide.
Loko was foiled by Atmatsidis early in the second half but made amends 10 minutes from time when he finished off a solo run in great style.
"It was by far our best away match this season. I am very happy with my three goals," said Loko.
Ricardo, PSG's Brazilian manager, said: "All our plans worked. We controlled the match after the first goal but I never believed we would end with such a wide victory.
"This match is a positive turning point and I believe the crisis in PSG is over."
AEK coach Petros Ravousis gave credit to the French side, saying: "PSG proved that it remains a big club despite their problems,". "They deserved the win."
